summary: Pole lookout tower on Mount Pulaski above Wallace, Idaho, built 1934 and abandoned 1946; only footings and a 1958 benchmark remain on the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Idaho Fire Lookouts writer says a vehicle reached the site in 2025; WillhiteWeb (2026) says the driving route stops within half a mile and the last part is an ATV track. Both are reported in the story; the route may have changed or the two parties may have used different tracks.

WillhiteWeb says the USGS placed the 1958 benchmark and wrote the description calling the station destroyed; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1958 station description attributed to the Coast and Geodetic Survey. Not reconciled; the story reports both.
Elevation is 5,488 ft on the firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts pages and 5,483 ft on WillhiteWeb. No elevation field is stored, so none is used in the story.

notes_for_editor: Built 1934 and abandoned 1946 agree across all four pages. Staff names come only from the Idaho Fire Lookouts page, which cites the Wallace Press-Times for Manning and Milot; the newspaper was not read. Access was recorded as unknown in the brief and is now restricted, because the summit route crosses private timber land and hiking is allowed for now by the company. The WillhiteWeb page has captioned photos but no image URLs in the cached text, so no new photos were added.
